clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old female presented with uncontrolled hypertension, angina, malaise, and fatigue, along with a significant differential blood pressure and pulse discrepancy. MR angiography revealed complete thrombosis of the left subclavian and left common carotid arteries, and severe luminal narrowing of the lower thoracic and abdominal aorta. Inflammatory markers (ESR and CRP) were elevated. The patient underwent percutaneous angioplasty for coronary artery disease, a complication likely related to the vasculitis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with uncontrolled hypertension, angina, malaise, fatigue, and differential blood pressure and pulse discrepancy (150/77 mm Hg in left arm vs 179/95 mm Hg in right arm; weak left radial pulse vs full right radial pulse).
MR angiography showed complete thrombosis of the left subclavian and left common carotid arteries, and 80-90% luminal narrowing of the long segmental lower thoracic and abdominal aorta.
Patient underwent percutaneous angioplasty with drug-eluting stents in LAD and LCX coronaries and was put on dual antiplatelet therapy.

remaining_uncertainties: Specific immunosuppressive treatment initiated for Takayasu Vasculitis was not reported.
Long-term clinical course or outcome related to the vasculitis activity.
